Here are some photos, maps or figures I have made:

Click any image to see it full size with its description; use the arrows to browse.

::: gallery
![Usumacinta basin, MODIS composite](assets/images/CuencaUsumacinta.jpg){group="figs" description="Cloudless MODIS composite (2015 - 2017) of the Usumacinta basin and surrounding areas. Figure was made in collaboration with C. Peralta-Carreta and can be seen in the Museo de Historia Natural, CDMX, Mexico"}

![Texture models vs. random expectation](assets/images/ModelsvsRandom.png){group="figs" description="Goodness-of-fit of the best models (black points) and its corresponding maximum goodness-of-fit distribution expected at random (boxes) for each tropical dry forest attribute (structural and diversity). Models were constructed using GLCM texture metrics calculated from multispectral bands (MS) and panchromatic (Pan) as explanatory variables. Figure from Solórzano et al. (2017)."}

![Observed vs. modeled: swamp forest](assets/images/FOTO_GLCMmodels.jpeg){group="figs" description="Observed versus modeled values and its corresponding linear fit (dashed line) of the best model for each vegetation attribute (ln-transformed) of a Tropical Swamp Forest. Models were fitted using image GLCM texture metric as explanatory variables. Figure from Solórzano et al. (2018)."}

![RDA ordination of species abundance](assets/images/RDA_DendrogramCometa.jpg){group="figs" description="RDA ordination showing the scores of the species abundance (gray letters), plots (black numbers) and environmental proxies (black letters) according to the RDA first two principal axes; although, the second axis was not significant. Environmental proxies included distance to water bodies and microtopography variables. Figure from Solórzano et al. (2020)."}

![Tree cover loss, Usumacinta 2000–2016](assets/images/Deforestation_GFCSerieINEGI.jpeg){group="figs" description="Tree cover area lost between 2000 and 2016 according to the Global Forest Change data in the Usumacinta River basin. Data are grouped by land cover / land use (Serie II, INEGI 2001) and part of the basin (low, mid, high). Figure from Peralta-Carreta et al. (2019)."}

![Landsat image availability in Mexico](assets/images/LandsatMX.jpg){group="figs" description="Number of available Landsat (4-8) images by path (upper border) and row (right border) of Mexico's surface between 1972 - 2017. Additionally, the percentage of images by cloud cover percentage is shown by the bar color. Figure from Solórzano et al. (2020)."}

![Sampling plots, Ayuquila basin](assets/images/Mapa_ZE_Ayuquila.jpg){group="figs" description="Plots location where conserved and degraded tropical dry forest was sampled in the Ayuquila River basin. Figure from Gao et al. (2020)."}

![U-Net land cover map](assets/images/unetpred.jpg){group="figs" description="Land use land cover map obtained using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery and a U-net architecture. Figure from Solórzano et al. (2021)."}

![RGB hillshade of Mexico](assets/images/Mexico_hillshade_final.png){group="figs" description="RGB hillshade of Mexico."}

![Mexico's highest peaks in 3D](assets/images/Volcanos_all_final.png){group="figs" description="Mexico's highest peaks - 3D plot (missing the Nevado de Colima)."}

![Deforestation detection: U-Net vs. SVM](assets/images/unetdefor.jpg){group="figs" description="Comparison among different deforestation detection methods using U-Net and SVM with Sentinel-2 (MS) and -1 images (SAR)"}

![NDVI time-series breaks with BFAST](assets/images/bfast.jpeg){group="figs" description="Example of four NDVI time series where changes were detected using BFAST"}

![Spectrogram thresholds and acoustic index](assets/images/spectro.png){group="figs" description="Spectrograms obtained using different thresholds (columns) for three different hours (rows) and its effect over a acoustic diversity index (final row)"}

![Avocado land-use trajectories (CCDC)](assets/images/trajanalysis.jpeg){group="figs" description="Trajectory analysis for land use land cover change associated with avocado orchards using CCDC and landsat images"}

![LiDAR aboveground biomass](assets/images/Map2.jpeg){group="figs" description="Aboveground biomass predictions and its variation based on LiDAR metrics (ALS) using a random forest algorithm."}

![Avocado pathways](assets/images/AvocadoPathways.jpg){group="figs" description="Land use land cover changes associated with avocado expansion. Two main pathways are indicated: crop substitution and deforestation."}

![CCDC vs. LandTrendr: forest disturbances](assets/images/CcdcvsLandtrendr.jpeg){group="figs" description="Comparison of CCDC and Landtrendr algorithms for mapping temperate forest disturbances."}
:::
